title: Short Active Duty Periods and the Family-Adjustment Relief
content:
**Training questions - TRICARE Premium-Based Plans, TRICARE Reserve Select.**

**Rule.** Active duty days count toward the family-adjustment relief only as the length of that coverage allows: where the active duty enrollment shows its coverage running more than 30 days from its effective date, those days count from the enrollment's effective date; where it shows its coverage running 30 days or fewer, no day counts; otherwise days count only after the plan's termination date.

**How is it read?** The active duty enrollment is the purchaser's applied or active TRICARE Prime Active Duty Service Member enrollment; its length is the number of days from its effective date to the coverage end date (disenrollment date) its record shows. "Otherwise" covers no such enrollment, or one whose record shows no coverage end date.

**What does each outcome do?** More than 30 days: no day before the enrollment's effective date counts. 30 days or fewer: no day counts. Otherwise: no day on or before the plan's termination date counts.

| Effective date | Coverage end shown | Length | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 June | 24 July | 30 days | no day counts |
| 24 June | 25 July | 31 days | days count from 24 June |
| 24 June | none | - | days count only after the plan's termination date |
